Class VirtualViewRMI

java.lang.Object
java.rmi.server.RemoteObject
java.rmi.server.RemoteServer
java.rmi.server.UnicastRemoteObject
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.server.network.rmi.VirtualViewRMI
All Implemented Interfaces:
ClientConnection, Listener, RmiServerService, Closeable, Serializable, AutoCloseable, Remote
public class VirtualViewRMI extends UnicastRemoteObject implements RmiServerService, ClientConnection, Listener
Dedicated RMI remote session for a single connected client.

Instances of this class are created by RmiConnectionEntryPoint when a client connects, before any authentication takes place. This class acts as a private proxy for the client on the server, maintaining its session id and holding the remote reference to its personal callback receiver (RmiClientService).

It is responsible for intercepting inbound client commands, delegating routing to the central MessageRouter, and dispatching outbound server updates back to the client via RMI callbacks.

      public void handleClientMessage(ClientMessage clientMessage) throws RemoteException
      Description copied from interface: RmiServerService
      Sends one application command message from the client to the server.

      The message contains the protocol type and the client-to-server payload. The server-side implementation uses the session associated with this remote object and routes the message through the normal server pipeline.

      Specified by:

    • sendPing

      public void sendPing()
      Description copied from interface: ClientConnection
      Sends a keep-alive ping to the remote client using the concrete transport.

      The ping-pong routine calls this method periodically for sessions that are still considered active. The corresponding pong is later recorded through the virtual view and server lifecycle.

      Specified by:
      sendPing in interface ClientConnection

    • pong

      public void pong(PongPayload payload) throws RemoteException
      Description copied from interface: RmiServerService
      Sends a keep-alive PONG reply from the client to the server.

      This method is separate from RmiServerService.handleClientMessage(ClientMessage) because the ping-pong protocol is connection-level infrastructure, not a user command. The server uses it to record that the client is still alive.

      Specified by:
      pong in interface RmiServerService
      Parameters:
      payload - keep-alive reply payload
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the remote session cannot receive the PONG

    • closeSession

      public void closeSession() throws RemoteException
      Description copied from interface: RmiServerService
      Closes the server-side session associated with this client.

      The client calls this during normal shutdown. The server-side implementation disconnects the session from the controller and unexports the remote session object so that it is no longer available through RMI.

      Specified by:
      closeSession in interface RmiServerService
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the remote close call cannot be delivered
